prompt: Why does `WeekUiState` compute `totalMinutes` from `sessions` instead of storing it as a field?
hint: Section 02 opens with a screen showing 90 beside a list adding up to 135.

choices.text: So the total can never disagree with the list
choices.why: Right: a value computed from the list follows every change to it, and nothing can forget to update it.

choices.text: Because a data class cannot hold an `Int` beside a `List`
choices.why: A data class holds any mix of fields; the choice is about consistency.

choices.text: To make the screen recompose less often
choices.why: A computed property changes nothing about when the screen recomposes; the state is replaced either way.

choices.text: Because `SavedStateHandle` cannot store numbers
choices.why: The handle stores numbers fine, and the total is not in the handle at all.

prompt: `draftMinutes` is a `String`. What would go wrong if it were an `Int`?
hint: Think about the field while the student is half-way through typing.

choices.text: Nothing, an `Int` would only use less memory
choices.why: An empty field and `"4"` on the way to `"45"` are states an `Int` cannot represent faithfully.

choices.text: An empty or half-typed field could not be shown
choices.why: Right: the text being typed is not yet a number, so it is kept as text and converted once, in `canAdd` and `onAdd`.

choices.text: `OutlinedTextField` would refuse to compile
choices.why: It would compile with a conversion at the call; the problem shows up when somebody types.

choices.text: The total would be computed in hours
choices.why: The unit has nothing to do with the type of the draft.

prompt: The ViewModel keeps a private `MutableStateFlow` and exposes it as a read-only `___`, so that only it can change the state.
hint: The type `asStateFlow()` returns.

prompt: In the planner, what does `WeekScreen` do when the student ticks a session's checkbox?
hint: State goes down, events come up.

choices.text: Calls `onToggleDone(id)` and draws whatever state comes back
choices.why: Right: the screen reports the intention and never changes the session itself.

choices.text: Sets `session.done = true` in the list it was given
choices.why: `done` is a `val` in an immutable class, and editing the given state is exactly what one-way flow forbids.

choices.text: Keeps the tick in a `remember` until the ViewModel catches up
choices.why: That is the second copy of the truth section 03 warns about.

choices.text: Writes the tick to the `SavedStateHandle`
choices.why: The screen never touches the handle; only the ViewModel does.

prompt: Why does the lesson split the screen into `WeekScreen` and `WeekRoute`?
hint: Which of the two did the screenshot test call?

choices.text: Because a composable may only take four parameters
choices.why: There is no such limit; `WeekScreen` takes five.

choices.text: So one part draws from any value and one part wires
choices.why: Right: the test drew `WeekScreen` from a state it made up; only `WeekRoute` touches the ViewModel.

choices.text: Because `viewModel()` cannot be called inside a `Column`
choices.why: It can be called in any composable; the split is about what each part depends on.

choices.text: So that the activity can choose a different ViewModel per rotation
choices.why: The same ViewModel is kept across rotation, which is section 04's point.

prompt: The screenshot test drew three sessions of 45, 25 and 90 minutes. What total did the screen show, in minutes?
hint: Add them.

prompt: A colleague makes `onDraftChange` ignore any keystroke that is not a digit, by not changing the state. What does the student see when typing a letter?
hint: Whose value does the field show?

choices.text: The letter appears, and disappears at the next recomposition
choices.why: The field never holds text of its own, so there is nothing to show the letter before the state changes.

choices.text: The app crashes, because the field and the state disagree
choices.why: They cannot disagree: the field shows `state.draftMinutes` and nothing else.

choices.text: Nothing changes in the field: the letter is refused
choices.why: Right: the field draws the state; a state that did not change draws the same text.

choices.text: The letter is kept and converted to 0 by `toIntOrNull`
choices.why: `toIntOrNull` gives `null` for a letter, and the letter never reached the state anyway.

prompt: `RecreateTest` printed the identities before and after `recreate()`. Which changed?
hint: Two different activities, one…

choices.text: Both: a new activity and a new ViewModel
choices.why: Then the session would have been lost, and the test found 45 minutes after the recreation.

choices.text: Only the activity
choices.why: Right: the activity is a new object and the ViewModelStore handed the old ViewModel to it.

choices.text: Only the ViewModel
choices.why: It is the other way round: recreation replaces the activity and keeps the ViewModel.

choices.text: Neither, because Robolectric does not recreate
choices.why: It does: the activity's identity changed.

prompt: Match where a value lives to the first event that loses it.
hint: The table in section 04.

pairs.right: the process killed in the background

right_distractors: a new version of the app installed

prompt: What does the `ViewModelStore` do when its activity is destroyed for good, not by a configuration change?
hint: The store is kept only across a configuration change.

choices.text: Hands its ViewModels to the next activity that opens
choices.why: It hands them on only across a configuration change; otherwise there is no successor.

choices.text: Writes its ViewModels into the saved `Bundle`
choices.why: Only `SavedStateHandle` values reach the `Bundle`; a ViewModel is never serialised.

choices.text: Calls `onCleared()` on each ViewModel and empties itself
choices.why: Right: that is the end of a ViewModel's life.

choices.text: Keeps them until the process ends
choices.why: They are cleared with the activity, which is why `ProcessDeathTest` got a new one.

prompt: After `ProcessDeathTest` rebuilt the activity from the `Bundle`, what came back?
hint: `after:` in the output.

choices.text: The draft "30", and no session
choices.why: Right: the draft was in the handle and the session only in the old ViewModel's memory.

choices.text: The session, and an empty draft
choices.why: The session was never written to the handle, so nothing could bring it back.

choices.text: Both, because the ViewModel was the same
choices.why: The test printed `same ViewModel: false`.

choices.text: Neither: the Bundle is empty after `destroy()`
choices.why: The Bundle was filled by `saveInstanceState` before `destroy()`, and the draft came back.

prompt: Which of these belongs in a `SavedStateHandle`?
hint: What the student was in the middle of, never the data itself.

choices.text: Every study session of the semester
choices.why: That is data; it belongs in a database, and a large Bundle fails with `TransactionTooLargeException`.

choices.text: The id of the course on screen
choices.why: Right: small, and enough to reload everything else.

choices.text: The activity, so it can be restored as it was
choices.why: An activity is not something a Bundle can hold, and holding one is section 06's leak.

choices.text: The rendered screen as a bitmap
choices.why: A bitmap is large and is redrawn from the state anyway.

prompt: A student types 45, switches to a video app for an hour, and comes back. The phone had killed the planner's process. Which statement describes what they see?
hint: Section 05 imitated exactly this in a test.

choices.text: The app opens on its first screen with nothing typed
choices.why: The system recreates the activity with its Bundle, and the draft is in it.

choices.text: The same screen with 45 in the field, and the sessions added before it gone
choices.why: Right: the handle survives the process and this lesson's in-memory list does not; lesson 15 fixes the second half.

choices.text: Everything exactly as it was, because the ViewModel was kept
choices.why: A ViewModel lives in the process's memory and dies with it.

choices.text: A crash, because the ViewModel's state is null
choices.why: A new ViewModel is built with a default state and the handle's draft; nothing is null.

prompt: Why does `LeakyViewModel`, holding the activity's `Context`, leak memory?
hint: Which of the two lives longer?

choices.text: Because `getString` copies every resource into the ViewModel
choices.why: `getString` returns one string; the problem is the reference kept in the field.

choices.text: Because a `Context` cannot be garbage-collected at all
choices.why: A `Context` is collected like anything else once nothing refers to it.

choices.text: The ViewModel outlives the activity and keeps the destroyed one reachable
choices.why: Right: after a rotation the old activity and its whole view tree stay in memory.

choices.text: Because lint marks it, and marked code is kept by R8
choices.why: Lint and R8 are unrelated; lint only reported the problem.

prompt: Lint reported the leaky field under the check called `___`.
hint: It is in square brackets at the end of the warning.

prompt: How does the planner put "160 min this week" on screen without the ViewModel touching resources?
hint: Values from one side, text from the other.

choices.text: The ViewModel keeps an `Application` and formats with it
choices.why: The course names `AndroidViewModel` and does not use it, to keep the ViewModel testable with no Android.

choices.text: The state carries the numbers and `WeekScreen` formats them with `stringResource`
choices.why: Right: the ViewModel produces values and the screen produces text, in the phone's language.

choices.text: The string is hard-coded in English in the state
choices.why: Then no other language could ever show it; lesson 1 section 07 warns against exactly that.

choices.text: The activity formats it and passes it to the ViewModel
choices.why: Text flows down from the screen's own resources; the ViewModel never receives it.

prompt: Why can `WeekViewModelTest` run with no Robolectric?
hint: Look at the ViewModel's imports.

choices.text: Because Gradle skips Android for tests in the `ui` package
choices.why: A package name changes nothing; what the class depends on does.

choices.text: Because the ViewModel holds no Android object
choices.why: Right: plain Kotlin over a `StateFlow`, built with a `SavedStateHandle` from a map.

choices.text: Because `testDebugUnitTest` always uses Robolectric anyway
choices.why: Only tests marked `@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)` get it; this one is plain JUnit.

choices.text: Because ViewModels are stubbed on the JVM
choices.why: The real `ViewModel` class ran; nothing was stubbed.

prompt: Which of these survive the process being killed in the background? Choose all that apply.
hint: Only what reached the Bundle, or the disk.

choices.text: A value in `rememberSaveable`
choices.why: Yes: it is saved into the Bundle.

choices.text: A field of the ViewModel
choices.why: No: the ViewModel dies with the process.

choices.text: A key in `SavedStateHandle`
choices.why: Yes: that is what the handle is for.

choices.text: A value in a plain `remember`
choices.why: No: it does not even survive a rotation.

prompt: A new screen needs the course name in the title. The ViewModel has the course id. Where should the id-to-name lookup's result end up?
hint: One state for one screen.

choices.text: In a field of the UI state, computed by the ViewModel
choices.why: Right: everything the screen draws is in its state, and the ViewModel makes it.

choices.text: In a `remember` inside the screen, looked up on first draw
choices.why: That is a second copy of the truth, lost on rotation, and the screen doing work it should not.

choices.text: In the `SavedStateHandle`, beside the id
choices.why: The handle holds the id; the name is data that can be looked up again from it.

choices.text: In the activity, passed to `setContent`
choices.why: The activity is recreated on rotation and would need to look it up again; the state is where it belongs.
